decision: Keep litestream-timestamp as the ObjectStoreConfig default and allow callers to select a provider-safe key.
why: This preserves existing S3/GCS and Litestream interoperability while enabling Azure metadata without a global rename.
evidence: Commit 896c5393af5e5b97ff930e1b3978627b3175f20c; default and Azure-only celld-ltx suites passed.

decision: Validate an empty timestamp metadata key before resolving or invoking the object store.
why: The prerequisite must fail before storage mutation and remain testable through injected provider-neutral stores.
evidence: Recording-store tests proved single and multipart dispatch, exact bytes and metadata, and zero operations for an empty key; both exact-delta reviews passed.

decision: Add az:// through the existing bucket and provider-neutral LTX seams with explicit account-key, SAS, and Azurite selection.
why: This keeps the upstream patch focused, prevents implicit identity fallback, and preserves S3/GCS behavior.
evidence: Commit f8afab8fbf39dfee6c9f25e6e0230bea10231796; default, Azure-only, internal-compile, Azurite, and exact-fix gates passed.

decision: Use nonempty Azure ETags for CAS, zero retries for conditional writes, and the public client-side list-offset fallback.
why: These are the existing fencing semantics and the accepted object-store 0.11.2 correctness path.
evidence: Development TME real Azure: 6/6 LTX tests, 2/2 CAS/prefix tests, 64-object bounded seek in 68ms, and counter restored from n=1 to n=2 after local cell DB deletion/restart.

decision: Use stable official Azure SDK credentials with explicit modes, exact Storage scope, and a coalesced five-minute refresh cache.
why: This preserves the accepted Azure storage contract while making Entra selection production-safe and reviewable as a separate patch.
evidence: Commit 1da23e7a7180b389b15d421d07adee590d7f56c0; developer tools, system/user-assigned managed identity, AKS workload identity deploy/run/diagnose/recovery, and same-pod projected-token rotation passed.

decision: Record client-secret live qualification as tenant-policy constrained rather than adding a fallback or nonapproved credential.
why: The tenant permits compliant app registration but rejects password credentials with CredentialTypeNotAllowedAsPerAppPolicy; changing the auth contract would weaken the approved design.
evidence: Committed tests cover construction, required variables, Blob scope, and no fallback; the temporary app and service principal created by the test were removed.

decision: Use the operator-approved AKS override with two isolated three-node fleets, stable private peer Services, workload identity, and one RWO Azure Disk per node.
why: This supplies the Azure-hosted multi-node oracle while matching the user's intended AKS deployment environment and preserving private peer identity.
evidence: Both fleets survived forced owner loss and local-cell deletion at epoch 2; old owners returned empty and nonresident. A 120-request cross-node fault run produced contiguous n=12..131, then n=132 and n=133 across epoch 3 takeover and stale-owner return.

decision: Classify only Azure condition service codes as clean CAS rejection and keep all other failures ambiguous with zero CAS retry.
why: Status alone can misclassify unrelated 409/412 responses and convert a possibly committed write into an unsafe rejection.
evidence: Commit 679fe33585648d9cf3fcade35a80725f574d9b20; raw Azure HTTP tests prove service-code mapping, one CAS attempt under 429/5xx, the ordinary three-attempt budget, and lost-response ambiguity.

decision: Qualify live loss of Blob connectivity with a pod-scoped Cilium egress fault rather than reconfiguring Azure Storage.
why: This exercises the real node lease watchdog and recovery path without modifying pre-existing or shared Azure service configuration.
evidence: The node returned one bounded ambiguous renewal, self-fenced in 16 seconds with exit code 3, and an empty replacement restored acknowledged n=1..3 as n=4 at epoch 2.
